text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) has started regular passenger flights between Copenhagen and Minsk, capital of Belarus, the company's Moscow office said on Tuesday.
SAS operates a 105-seat DC-9-41 jet making the trip three days a week on Mondays, Thursdays and Fridays.

"We have noticed a growing interest in Belarus from the Scandinavian business community...and we are expecting this route to also attract passengers from the rest of Europe," the statemnet quoted SAS route manager Per Soderblom as saying.
Currently, SAS operates regular flights from Stockholm to Moscow (14 flights a week), to St Petersburg (11 flights) and Kaliningrad (four flights).
Earlier this year, Gunther Sollinger, SAS general manager Russia CIS, said SAS planned to open one new destination in Russia a year during 1997-1999, but he did not name them.
He also said the average passenger load factor on the airline's flights to Russia was about 60 percent.
